Supercapacitors
Liqiong Zhang,
[a, b]

Supercapacitors with the performance advantages of high-
power density are emerging materials for energy storage/
conversion systems that can combat climate change caused by
CO
2
emissions and are of importance with the development of
electronic products and artificial intelligence. But rationally
preparing high-performance electrode with high mass-loading
quantity remains challenge. Herein, we have opted for chitosan
as well-structured binding agent to combine with active carbon
(SSP-900), a 3D hierarchical micro-meso-macro porous biochar
previously obtained, to synthesize high mass-loading freestand-
ing electrode. Especially, the freestanding material (C
1000
G
0.2
),
owning 0.2 g SSP-900 and suffering carbonization at 1000 ° C
exhibits high specific surface area of 389.3 cm

electrical energy from intermittent solar and wind.
Introduction
With the development of electronic products and artificial
intelligence, a global consensus has been formed to address
climate change caused by CO
2
emissions. For that, the power
generation system, mainly sustained by fossil fuels, should be
replaced with low CO
2
emissions and sustainable energy
sources like water and tide.
[1]
Nevertheless, the intermittent
feature of clean energy remains a gap in integrating the instant
powering system.
[2]
On the contrary, electrochemical technol-
ogy in energy storage/conversion systems has been widely
considered one of the most efficacious strategies to step over
the gap.
[3]
In that, Li-ions batteries, Na-ions batteries, fuel
batteries, and super-capacitors are the four most important
energy storage/conversion patterns.
[4–5]
Especially the super-
capacitors, generally exhibiting feature with high power energy,
superb cycle stability, and quick charge and discharge, has
been picked as a strong candidate for energy conversion and
storage systems.
[6]
Typically, the electrode material has a vital influence on energy
density, even is the key winning point for super-capacitors.
Furthermore, electrode materials are always powder, which does
not tend to perfect conductivity and adhesion.
[7–8]
Although the
binder and additive assist addition can further improve excellent
electrochemical performance, the microstructure and micromor-
phology of electrode materials, especially the nano-scale, could be
greatly affected by the stack or shrink.
[9]
In addition, there is an
important note that the low active material loading with 1–2 mg
on working electrode tends to be overestimated on specific
capacitance and energy density, which may exist difficulty in
practical application.
[10]
Based on it, a freestanding electrode
material like graphene flakes,
[11,12]
and MXene flakes,
[13,14]
with high
specific surface area, strong conductivity, and flexibility, is being
emerged in research. Unfortunately, these two-dimensional
materials are prone to producing a stacking phenomenon during
the working process, which has a disgusting impact on electro-
chemical performance.
[15]
Also, the high preparation cost makes
their practical application a great barrier.
[16]
To resolve the
immediate issue, the studies have focused on biomass resources
because they exhibit the important merits of sustainable energy
with low-cost, and constant supply and storage.
[17–20]
Thus,
preparing freestanding bio-based electrode materials is both
important and fruitful for the development of supercapacitor in
energy storage.
Chitosan, as a kind of renewable natural polymer with a
linear special structure, can be dissolved in an acidic aqueous
solution to form a gel. And the chitosan aerogel possesses

temperature carbonization, and it could be a candidate material
in theoretical for freestanding electrodes.
[20]
But, there remains a
high volume of waste in lightweight carbonization chitosan
gels, due to structural characteristics with high macrospores
content, which is not conducive to storing ion energy.
[21,22]
And
excessively increasing the amount of chitosan will be a high-
costly behavior. Generally, materials with mixing or doping are
capable of achieving many technologically functional properties
that may not be easily accessible in a traditional single material,
and then it has been attracting significant interest in various
fields, such as photocatalysis,
[23,24]
high-temperature
superconductivity,
[25,26]
piezoelectricity.
[27,28]
Interestingly, the
synergistic contribution of the special pore structure and
internal atom (N and O) of soybean-based carbon powder
material has been prepared, which is called SSP-900 in our
previous studies as shown in Figure S1. And the SSP-900 has
been favorable to generating splendid electrochemical perform-
ance (357 F g
� 1
) in the supercapacitor field.
[29]
Given the excellent structural characteristics of chitosan as
well as our previous research on the soybean-based carbon
powder material, we chose chitosan and SSP-900 as binder and
additive respectively. The freestanding electrode material with
high conductivity, lightweight, independent frame, and high
specific surface area were synthesized. Chitosan completely
wrapped the SSP-900 in the frame, meanwhile, the prepared
freestanding materials have mass of 6 mg on average. Further-
more, various properties of obtained were tested, especially the
electrochemical properties. The superior sample (C
1000
G
0.2
),
containing 0.2 g SSP-900 and carbonization at 1000 ° C, has
shown an exciting electrochemical property with a large specific
capacitance of 65 F g
� 1
, a high energy density of 32.5 Wh kg
� 1
under the power density of 90.4 W kg
� 1
. And after 10,000 cycles
at a current density of 2 A g
� 1
, it remains excellent capacitance
stability (98 %). This research also provides an effective
approach for preparing freestanding electrode materials in the
field of supercapacitors.

Experimental Section
Materials
Chitosan (Degree of deacetylation 95 %), Polyethylene polypropy-
lene glycol (P123, Mn 5800), dl-lactic acid (Mw 90.08), and
potassium hydroxide (KOH, GR 95 %) were all purchased from
Macklin company without any further purification.
Synthesis of carbon aerogel
1 g of chitosan was completely dissolved in 25 mL of acidic
aqueous solution (0.5 mL of dl-Lactic acid) with continuous stirring
for 15 min. On the other hand, 1 g of P123 was added to 15 mL of
deionized water to thoroughly disperse. Different quantities of SSP-
900 (0, 0.1, 0.2, 0.3 g) were evenly mixed with the mixture solution
of the above chitosan solution and two P123 solutions to form
hydrogels, respectively. The detailed preparation process for SSP-
900 was described in the previous work.
[29]
Following, the hydrogels
were shaped using a plastic mold (D = 18 mm) and they were let to
stand for 2 h until the bubbles overflowed. The plastic molds were
placed in the refrigerator to freeze for 12 h and then transferred to
a desiccator for drying to form aerogel. Subsequently, the obtained
aerogels were pyrolyzed at different temperatures (900, 1000,
1100 ° C) keeping 2 h at the rate of 5 ° C min
� 1
to get freestanding
carbon materials. For simplicity of expression, we denoted the got
freestanding materials as C
x
G
y
, where x is the carbonization
temperature, and y is the quality of SSP-900 in the mixing process.
In this process, the interwoven gel structure of chitosan constituted
the framework of freestanding carbon materials and was filled up
by the SSP-900 with a high specific surface area. And P123, as an
organic templating agent, could effectively break thick layer
barriers on the gel structure at high temperatures to improve the
porosity.
[57]
